devdoc.author: Ananya Aastha — N12125547 | IFB452 Blockchain Technology, QUT
devdoc.details: Architecture overview:  Stakeholders  →  HealthRecords Smart Contract  →  IPFS (off-chain encrypted storage)  Six stakeholders:   1. Patient          — owns records, manages all consent   2. Doctor / GP      — reads and adds records with patient consent   3. Hospital         — same as doctor, also registers emergency personnel   4. Pharmacist       — reads and marks prescriptions as dispensed   5. Insurer          — read-only with explicit patient consent   6. Regulator        — admin-level read of anonymised audit data  Novel features vs MedRec (Azaria et al., 2016):   1. Auto-expiry consent  — permissions revoke automatically at block.timestamp   2. Emergency override with penalty mechanism — strikes + suspension on misuse

PatientAlerted(address,address,uint256,u.details: NOVEL — patient is immediately alerted when emergency access occurs

ProviderPenalised(address,uint256,bool,u.details: NOVEL — penalty mechanism for unjustified emergency access

addRecord(address,string,bytes32,uint8).details: Caller must be: patient themselves | consented doctor | consented pharmacist

params._fileHash: keccak256 hash of the file for integrity verification
params._ipfsHash: IPFS CID of the encrypted file

emergencyAccess(address,string).details: Issues a 4-hour read-only token. Patient is immediately alerted on-chain.      Every access is permanently logged for governance review.

getRecords(address).details: Access: patient | consented doctor | consented pharmacist |              consented insurer | emergency personnel

grantConsent(address,uint256).details: Consent auto-expires at block.timestamp >= expiryTime — no patient action needed

reviewAccess(uint256,bool,string).details: If unjustified, penalisePersonnel is called automatically

params._eventId: The emergency event ID to review
params._isJustified: Whether the access was clinically justified

params._fileHash: Hash to check against stored hash
params._recordIdx: Index in the patient's record array

@title HealthRecords
 @author Ananya Aastha — N12125547 | IFB452 Blockchain Technology, QUT
 @notice Decentralised Healthcare Record Sharing System (DHRSS)
 @dev Architecture overview:
  Stakeholders  →  HealthRecords Smart Contract  →  IPFS (off-chain encrypted storage)
  Six stakeholders:
   1. Patient          — owns records, manages all consent
   2. Doctor / GP      — reads and adds records with patient consent
   3. Hospital         — same as doctor, also registers emergency personnel
   4. Pharmacist       — reads and marks prescriptions as dispensed
   5. Insurer          — read-only with explicit patient consent
   6. Regulator        — admin-level read of anonymised audit data
  Novel features vs MedRec (Azaria et al., 2016):
   1. Auto-expiry consent  — permissions revoke automatically at block.timestamp
   2. Emergency override with penalty mechanism — strikes + suspension on misuse
@dev NOVEL — patient is immediately alerted when emergency access occurs
@dev NOVEL — penalty mechanism for unjustified emergency access
